title: Power Rankings: Unwrapping a new No. 1
heading: 2010-11 Power Rankings: Week 8
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: KG's resurrection. Pierce's clutchness and versatility. Overcoming every injury. The Celts are just overloading us, since we also can't stop reciting Barkley's priceless Rondo line: "He's the engine that stirs the drink."

rankings.summaryHtml: Their win streak and No. 1 ranking are gonzo, but the Mavs still have to feel decent about themselves. First they send Miami straight into that team meeting, then Phoenix makes a huge trade hours after a heavy L in Big D.

rankings.summaryHtml: Know this as you study up for Miami's full-circle showdown with Dallas: Fastbreak points looks like the key stat in any Heat box score. When they score at least 15 in transition, they're 12-2. Fewer than 15? Just 9-6.

rankings.summaryHtml: This week's safe bet: Bulls fans are cursing us after we guaranteed -- in writing -- that their squad was in the top 10 to stay ... only for Noah, on cue, to go down with a long-term wrist injury. Of course we feel responsible.

rankings.summaryHtml: We repeat: Can't shake the suspicion that the reconfigured Jazz require D-Will to carry a nightly load that's realistically too much to shoulder for a full 82 games. Hope we're wrong, 'cause he's off to a career-year start.

rankings.summaryHtml: If anyone in Orlando can feel good about an overhaul this dramatic -- which wouldn't have surprised our loyal readers -- it's the coach. Van Gundy must feel some pride that his bosses imploded the roster instead of ousting him.

rankings.summaryHtml: Not so surprised to see Grant Hill turn back the clock on the Thunder. The bigger surprise was seeing this season's kings of the close game fail to pull that one out: OKC's now 9-2 in games decided by five points or fewer.

rankings.summaryHtml: Did we overstate the Knicks' 13-2 run before their 0-3 plummet to Earth? We and everybody else. As my man Scott Howard-Cooper of NBA.com suggests, maybe we did need to focus more on the 13 teams they beat.

rankings.summaryHtml: One theory to explain the 8-3 revival beyond help from the schedule and Philly's  vastly improved D: Opposing teams can't lock in on the Sixers because even they aren't sure night-to-night where their O will come from.

rankings.summaryHtml: Our fondness for Bogut and (the now injured) Jennings makes it hard to give in here, but Milwaukee just doesn't score enough to be a top-five team in the East. The most galling part: No. 5 is still so up for grabs.

rankings.summaryHtml: No one's blaming Paul George, but facts is facts: Indy's tough schedule last week (Bulls, Lakers, Celtics) and resultant dip below .500 leaves Utah's Hayward and OKC's Aldrich as the only lottery picks on winning teams.

rankings.summaryHtml: The best basketball from last season's Grizzlies came after Christmas and lasted through January. Just not sure they have the mojo or chemistry to do it again after what we will say has been a road-heavy December schedule.
